spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The operative move is to reclassify the difficult Type II off-diagonal contributions as a multidimensional circle-method problem, so that convolution and rational approximation become a systematic language for lower-order terms rather than isolated corrections.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source approaches shifted and unshifted zeta moments by replacing zeta(s)^k with long Dirichlet polynomials and studying their mean square; the new task is a general treatment of Type II off-diagonal terms using a circle-method framework and convolutions of shifted divisor sums.
directed.conceptual_reading: The key reframing is that off-diagonal terms have organized multidimensional geometry. Treating them as circle-method strata suggests a reusable intermediate representation in which correlations can be separated and recombined.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Long Dirichlet polynomials bridge zeta moments to divisor correlations, while the multidimensional Hardy-Littlewood circle-method viewpoint bridges those correlations to rational-direction analysis.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span states the program and claimed scope but does not supply the correlation estimates or the derivation of all lower-order terms. Earlier Type I and special Type II successes do not by themselves establish the general case.
directed.uncertainty: The prose is clear and the central notation is legible; the mathematical status here is methodological positioning rather than a proved result.

supported: The span presents long Dirichlet polynomials and their mean squares as the route to zeta moments.
It explicitly reframes the Bogomolny-Keating treatment as a multidimensional Hardy-Littlewood circle method and states the goal of treating all Type II off-diagonal terms.
inference: Calling the reframing an organized geometry is a plausible interpretation of the multidimensional circle-method language.
unsupported_or_imported: Rational approximation, rational directions, and a stratification in which correlations are separated and recombined do not appear in this span; they are imported from later sections.
The claim that convolution and rational approximation replace isolated corrections is stronger than the introductory program statement.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The phrases 'organized multidimensional geometry' and 'circle-method strata' risk a generic structure-exposing gloss without a span-local operation.
missed_mechanism: The source's concrete contrast is historical and methodological: Type I terms and the simplest Type II cases were handled earlier, while systematic general Type II treatment is the present task.
revision_instructions: Keep the long-polynomial-to-mean-square bridge and the explicit multidimensional circle-method reframing, but remove rational-direction and strata claims from this unit.
State that this is programmatic positioning, with the actual Type II computation and lower-order-term derivation deferred.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Residue subtraction is the useful intermediate construction: it removes the poles crossed in Perron truncation so a finite, long Dirichlet polynomial can be compared to the intended shifted-zeta product without silently retaining truncation residues.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For shift sets A and B, the coefficients tau_A are defined by the Euler product D_A(s)=product over alpha in A of zeta(s+alpha). Perron inversion expresses the truncation D_A(s;X) as D_A(s), explicit pole residues R_A(s;X), and a shifted contour integral; the studied moment uses D_A(s;X)-R_A(s;X) on both sides.
directed.conceptual_reading: The pole-subtracted polynomial is a controlled surrogate rather than a naive truncation. It preserves the long-polynomial coefficient structure while separating singular contributions that would otherwise confound comparison with the full shifted moment.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Perron inversion is the bridge from the finite coefficient sum to the meromorphic shifted-zeta representation; the R_A and R_B terms record precisely what contour motion exposes and removes.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The assertion that X>T^k should recover the full shifted moment asymptotically is explicitly an expectation in this setup, not a theorem proved in the unit.
directed.uncertainty: Several displays are extraction-sensitive, so exact residue normalizations should be checked against the PDF before reuse; the roles of truncation and residue subtraction are clear.

supported: The definitions of tau_A, the truncated series, Perron representation, residue term R_A, and the pole-subtracted moment are accurately identified.
The expectation X>T^k is correctly kept distinct from a proved asymptotic.
inference: Describing residue subtraction as a controlled surrogate is a reasonable conceptual reading of the displayed construction.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: Calling D_A(s;X)-R_A(s;X) a 'pole-subtracted polynomial' or a finite long Dirichlet polynomial is imprecise: subtracting R_A adds meromorphic shifted-zeta residue terms to the finite coefficient sum.
context_or_ocr_risk: Exact residue normalizations and display transcription remain formula-sensitive, as the candidate notes.
missed_mechanism: Perron contour motion gives D_A(s;X)=D_A(s)+R_A(s;X)+a shifted-contour integral, so the subtraction cancels the explicitly crossed residues rather than producing another pure polynomial.
revision_instructions: Refer to D_A(s;X)-R_A(s;X) as a pole-subtracted truncation or comparison object, not as a polynomial.
Preserve the exact Perron decomposition and the conjectural status of the X>T^k expectation.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The same underlying pair (m,n) survives a large change of presentation. Expanding the shifted divisor sums into μ- and ν-factors, choosing distinguished factors, distributing the remaining factors among ℓ slots, and absorbing them into a rescaled (∗)-system creates many equation systems without changing m or n; counting this fiber recovers exactly the swap multiplicity.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source expands τ_A(m) and τ_B(n) through factorizations m=μ₁⋯μ_k and n=ν₁⋯ν_k, partitions the indices into ℓ blocks, and starts from equations Nⱼmⱼ=Mⱼnⱼ+hⱼ with ∏Mⱼ=∏Nⱼ. After selecting divisors μⱼ,νⱼ and writing complementary factors with hats, it rescales each equation to a new tilde system representing the same m,n. Assigning each of the k−ℓ unused μ-factors and ν-factors to one of ℓ slots gives ℓ^(k−ℓ) choices per side, and ordering the ℓ distinguished factors gives (ℓ!)², hence (ℓ!)²ℓ^(2(k−ℓ)).
directed.conceptual_reading: This is an invariance-under-refactorization argument. The equation system remembers how prime/divisor factors were routed through slots, whereas the original summand remembers only their total products m and n. Forgetting that routing exposes a redundant fiber whose size can be divided out.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the divisor-factor expansion, the index-block partition, and the rescaled tilde (∗)-system. They translate between a global summand indexed by (m,n) and local direction-discrepancy equations; the global product balance for the tilde coefficients preserves membership in the same class of systems.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The count is asserted to remain valid whether some hⱼ vanish, and common factors in a tilde coefficient pair may be divided from the equation. This is multiplicity bookkeeping, not a proof of the conjectural shifted-divisor evaluation or of the correctness of every resulting analytic term.
directed.uncertainty: OCR substantially confuses hats, stars, products, and exponents in the displayed formulas. The factor-allocation construction and final multiplicity are recoverable from the surrounding prose, but finer identities involving individual decorated variables should not be reconstructed from this span.

supported: The span expands the shifted divisor coefficients through factor variables, partitions their indices into ell blocks, and starts from an ell-equation star system with product-balanced coefficients.

It selects factors dividing the local m_j and n_j, forms a rescaled tilde system corresponding to the same total m and n, and notes that a common factor of a tilde coefficient pair must also be divided from the discrepancy.

Assigning each of the k-ell unused mu-factors and nu-factors among ell slots gives ell^(k-ell) choices per side; ordering the ell distinguished factors contributes (ell!)^2, matching the swap multiplicity.
The source explicitly says the count applies whether or not some h_j vanish and that the common multiplicity must be divided out.
inference: Calling the construction invariance under refactorization and viewing the routing data as a redundant fiber over (m,n) are reasonable abstractions of the same-total-products construction.
The statement that product balance keeps the rescaled equations in the same class is supported conceptually by the displayed product identity, although its decorated variables are OCR-fragile.
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase 'prime/divisor factors' imports primality: the span introduces factor variables mu_i and nu_i in product decompositions but does not say that they are prime.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Invariance under refactorization' and 'forgetting routing' would be generic without the concrete slot assignment, ordering, product-balance, and common-factor normalization; the candidate supplies most of those operations.
context_or_ocr_risk: Hats, stars, tildes, products, and exponents are visibly corrupted, and one displayed sentence has inconsistent decorated variables; claims about individual rescaling formulas should therefore remain below the level of exact symbol reconstruction.
The prose is nevertheless sufficient for the same-(m,n) claim, the allocation count, the permutation count, the treatment of zero discrepancies, and the final multiplicity.
missed_mechanism: The source-grounded and bridge fields do not foreground the common-factor normalization of each rescaled equation; it appears only in the boundary field even though it is part of the mechanism that returns a valid normalized star system.
revision_instructions: Replace 'prime/divisor factors' with 'factor variables' or 'divisor-factor variables.'

Move the common-factor division into the main construction summary, and describe the tilde rescaling and product balance at the prose-supported structural level rather than implying exact recovery of every OCR-damaged decorated identity.
